subject: ClarifyAI model fit & prompt harvest — next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Morris <danielle@clarityai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: ClarifyAI model fit & prompt harvest — next steps

Thanks again for the time today, Danielle — good conversation. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we can get an eval/pilot started: 

Summary of needs
- Primary feature: auto-extract structured ESG fields (section, metric, value, confidence) and produce short user-facing summaries for your analytics UI.
- Volume: ~12k doc pages/month initially; peak bursts during earnings windows.
- SLO: median generation latency <250ms for short extractions, 95th <800ms.
- Data sensitivity: mostly public filings + some client-uploaded files (PII present in a subset).

Model / configuration recommendations (initial)
- Recommendation A (low-latency): redwood/fastgen-13B-q4f16 — good latency/quality tradeoff for extraction tasks where cost matters.
- Recommendation B (best-quality): open-70b-rrhf (8-bit) with Redwood KV-caching — higher quality for long-context reasoning and table extraction.
- Recommendation C (safety fallback): small instruction-tuned model for heuristic extractions and redaction checks before passing to main model.

Benchmarks and artifacts
- I pushed our quick bench summary and sample eval page here: https://redwood-internal.s3.amazonaws.com/evals/clarityai/2026-07-30/summary.html (contains token-cost breakdown, latency percentiles, and sample outputs).
- Attached: clarityai_benchmarks_20260730.xlsx (quick breakdown by model variant) and call recording link.

Prompt harvest ask (what we need from you)
1) 200–300 representative user prompts / queries covering: normal flows, ambiguous language, and at least 40 labeled edge cases (examples with expected extraction fields). CSV preferred; see attached "clarity_prompt_intake_template.csv".
2) Mark any items that include PII and indicate whether you can provide anonymized versions. If not, we can perform redaction on our side given your consent.
3) A short list of acceptance criteria for correctness (e.g., exact match for metric codes vs. free-text allowed).

Redaction guidance
- Attached redaction checklist (redaction_checklist_v1.pdf) with recommended columns to strip/transform. If you already have a pipeline, tell us the format and we’ll adapt.

Next steps / owners
- From Redwood: Marissa will run the initial model-fit eval once we receive the prompt set (ETA 5 business days after upload). Neha will prepare quantized runs and provide cost/latency projections.
- From ClarifyAI: Danielle — please confirm timeline for data share, and whether procurement needs to be looped for a pilot statement of work.

Proposed timeline
- Data upload window: by Aug 6 (2 weeks)
- Bench + first-pass quality report: Aug 11
- Pilot kickoff (if all good): Aug 18

If this sounds right I’ll send the intake template and a secure upload link.

Cheers,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

Attachments: clarity_prompt_intake_template.csv, redaction_checklist_v1.pdf, clarityai_benchmarks_20260730.xlsx
From: Danielle Morris <danielle@clarityai.com>

Cc: procurement@clarityai.com
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 08:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: ClarifyAI model fit & prompt harvest — next steps

Thanks Ben — this is helpful and lines up with our internal readout. A few quick clarifications: 

1) Redaction: we can provide an anonymized slice (~150 examples) by next Tuesday but some legal review is needed before full dataset transfer. We typically remove names/emails and mask client account IDs (we can provide a mapping key under NDA).
2) Edge cases: we have a recurring issue where tables embed text in images (OCR errors) — should we include OCR output plus original image reference?
3) Procurement: looping them in for the pilot SOW is great; they’ve asked for a simple MSA + one-month pilot cost estimate.

For the onboarding CSV: can you confirm required columns and whether you accept hashed IDs? Also: is there a secure S3 upload or should we use the Drive link?

— Danielle
Danielle Morris
Head of Product, ClarifyAI
danielle@clarityai.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Morris <danielle@clarityai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, procurement@clarityai.com
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 08:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ClarifyAI model fit & prompt harvest — next steps

Danielle — perfect, thanks for the clarity. Quick answers: 
- Redaction/hash: hashed IDs are fine. If you can supply a mapping under NDA later that’s ideal for debugging; for the eval we can work with hashed values.
- OCR cases: include the OCR output as a separate column and attach a sample image reference if possible — that helps the model/eval pipeline differentiate OCR errors vs. model hallucination.
- Upload method: we’ll create a short-lived S3 bucket and a pre-signed upload link. Drive is OK for small CSVs, but S3 preferred for larger bundles. I’ll share the link in the next message.
- Procurement: Ben_K (procurement contact) at Redwood will send a one-page pilot SOW and pilot estimate today.

Plan: Marissa will spin up the eval once the sample upload is visible (she’ll run Recommendation A and B variants and produce a delta report). Neha will configure quantized runs for fastgen-13B and run cost projections. Expect an initial bench + QC report ~5 business days after dataset arrival.

Ben

Subject: ClarifyAI — intake template and secure upload

Hi Danielle — linking the intake artifacts and secure upload: 

- Intake template (attached): clarity_prompt_intake_template.csv — columns: sample_id, raw_prompt, ocr_text (optional), expected_entities (json-string), pii_flag, severity_tag, notes. We included examples in the file to show formatting.
- Redaction checklist attached: redaction_checklist_v1.pdf — follow the columns; hashed IDs OK.
- Secure upload: https://redwood-s3-presigned.example.com/clarityai-upload-20260731 (expires in 7 days). Please upload to that bucket and then reply here with the approximate number of files/rows so we can provision the eval runners.

Edge-case guidance: please include at least 25 samples where OCR output is intentionally noisy (we’ll mark these as edge-case buckets in the report). If you have images, include 1–2 sample images and note the OCR engine used.

We’ll start the benchmark on receipt. If you’d like us to perform an initial PII redaction pass before the upload, we can schedule that under an NDA — happy to scope that if needed.

Thanks — Marissa
